rules_sent_back.instruction: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a reviewer who is a different actor from the one who produced the work checks that work and assigns it one of two alternative outcomes, where one outcome sends the work back to an earlier actor to repeat it and the other outcome lets the process continue

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a check or review of an earlier work product ends in one of two outcomes, and each outcome is followed either by a further described action or by termination of the process: Model the check as a task in the lane of the party that performs it, and model the recording of its outcome as a separate task in that same lane. Place an exclusive gateway after the outcome task, with one branch per outcome. On each branch, model the described follow-up action as its own task, including any return to an earlier actor for repetition and any continuation to the next stage. Where the description gives no follow-up action for an outcome, route that branch directly to an end event named for that outcome. Do not merge the two outcomes, do not place the follow-up action before the gateway, and do not replace a described action with a bare sequence flow or an end event that carries the action's meaning.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a check or review of an earlier work product ends in one of two outcomes, and each outcome is followed either by a further described action or by termination of the process
rules_sent_back.source: learned guideline (refines PROC-04), generalized from EXS-022

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description has a sentence in which a party examines or writes an item, followed by a sentence in which a different party checks that work and may record an outcome for it, and each sentence names its own action and object: Model each described action as its own task, placed in the lane of the party named in its sentence. Label every task with the action and object of its own sentence, using the description's words. Do not label the examination or writing step with the wording of the later check or outcome step, and do not label the check or outcome step with the wording of the earlier step. Keep the check task and the outcome-recording task separate, and keep the examination and writing tasks even when a neighboring task uses similar wording.
